FOOTNOTES

2/ Pursuant to section 41-5741, Arizona Revised Statutes, the amount appropriated for new school facilities shall be used only for facilities and land costs for school districts that received final approval from the division of school facilities on or before December 15, 2025. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

3/ After approving a distribution of funding for a land purchase, a land lease or the construction of a new school, the division of school facilities shall report to the joint legislative budget committee and the governor's office of strategic planning and budgeting the final amount of the distribution. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

4/ The legislature intends that the appropriation to the division of school facilities in fiscal year 2027-2028 for new school facilities may include up to \$10,000,000 for end of useful life projects that receive final approval from the division of school facilities on or before December 15, 2026 pursuant to section 41-5741, Arizona Revised Statutes. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

5/ At least thirty days before any monies are transferred out of the new school facilities debt service line item, the division of school facilities shall report the proposed transfer to the director of the joint legislative budget committee. (General Appropriation Act footnote)

6/ Pursuant to section 35-142.01, Arizona Revised Statutes, any reimbursement received by or allocated to the division of school facilities under the federal qualified school construction bond program in fiscal year 2026-2027 shall be deposited in or revert to the state general fund. (General Appropriation Act footnote)

7/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by division.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$1,624,700 and 17.0 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the operating budget. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

New School Facilities

The Baseline includes \$132,947,300 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for New School Facilities, which is a decrease of \$(7,727,500) from FY 2026. The funding amount for New School Facilities includes the following:

\$94,137,900 for the remaining 50% of construction funding to complete 3 projects which were authorized to begin construction in FY 2026.

\$38,809,400 for one project funded in FY 2027 to resolve an Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) case brought against SFD by the Agua Fria Union High School District. This figure also includes \$1,832,200 of site conditions costs related to the same district.

All new school construction is labeled as one-time spending rather than ongoing spending. (See Table 3 for a summary of New School Facilities Funding)

Background – The New School Facilities line item provides funding for school districts to build new K-12 school facilities. The division distributes the monies to school districts as work is completed on approved projects. A school district qualifies for new construction funding when the districtwide square feet per student is predicted to fall below the statutory minimum within the next 2 years. Funding is then provided to the district at a statutorily-prescribed dollar amount per square foot.

The dollar amount per square foot is adjusted annually based on a construction market index identified by the JLBC.

At its planned January 2026 meeting, the JLBC may approve a 4.8% adjustment in the cost per square foot. This inflation adjustment would be based on a measure of construction costs since December 2024 when the Committee last adopted an adjustment. This assumed adjustment would apply to the FY 2027 projects approved by the division. (See Table 1 for the current statutory

funding amounts, which include the prospective January 2026 adjustment).

New School Facilities

In addition, the division distributes money for land acquisition and site conditions. Site conditions funding is used for extraordinary site-specific construction needs such as: 1) earth moving costs beyond normal requirements, such as dynamite blasting; 2) building footings that must be deeper than standard code (in excess of 3 feet below grade); and 3) replacing poor/collapsing soil which cannot support buildings with other materials such as engineered fill. Site conditions do not include the costs of utilities placement or complying with standard local building codes.

New School Facilities (FY 2024 Authorization)

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for New School Facilities projects which were authorized to start construction in FY 2024. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Background – The FY 2024 budget included funding for 7 projects, for which monies were distributed in FY 2024 and FY 2025:

Agua Fria (9-12) – for a new high school including land

• Liberty (K-8) – for a new elementary school including land.

Queen Creek (K-6) – for 2 elementary school additions.

Queen Creek (K-6) – for a new elementary school including land.

• Queen Creek (7-8) – for 2 middle school additions.

Saddle Mountain (9-12) – for a high school addition.

Snowflake (9-12) – for a new high school including land.

New School Facilities (FY 2025 Authorization)

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for New School Facilities projects which were authorized to start construction in FY 2025. Adjustments are as follows:

New School Funding Completion

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(45,077,100) from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the completion of 5 projects:

Maricopa (6-8) – for a new middle school and a land purchase

Queen Creek (9-12) – for 2 high school additions.

Sahuarita (9-12) – for high school addition and site conditions. The SFD award (and corresponding appropriated amount) for this project reflects a deduction of \$(484,900) for design costs previously funded.

Valentine (K-8) – for a replacement school, site conditions, and demolition. SFD has determined that Valentine Elementary School has outlived its useful life. Under statute, with that determination, SFD removed the school's capacity and recalculated the new construction square footage requirements based on total district enrollment and minimum adequacy guidelines. SFD then awarded the district a 15,463 square foot project.

New School Facilities (FY 2026 Authorization)

The Baseline includes \$94,137,900 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for New School Facilities projects which are authorized to start construction in FY 2026. Adjustments are as follows:

Continue New School Construction Projects

The Baseline includes an increase of \$538,600 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for New School Facilities projects. These school districts are projected to be at capacity in FY 2027 or before. The first half of construction costs and 100% of land costs for each project were funded in FY 2026. The FY 2026 General Appropriations Act advance appropriated the remaining 50% of construction costs for each project in FY 2027. The projects are as follows:

Laveen (K-8) – for a new elementary school including land.

Nadaburg (K-8) – for a new elementary school including a land donation credit.

Snowflake (7-8) – for a new middle school.

Tolleson (9-12) – for a new high school.

This adjustment also includes the removal of \$10,000,000 of one-time savings associated with project consolidations in FY 2026. The savings from these consolidations were realized by reducing SFD's FY 2026 New School Facilities appropriation.

The FY 2026 General Appropriations Act appropriated the remaining \$94,137,900 of funding in FY 2027 to fund the remaining 50% of construction costs for these projects. As a result, these monies will not appear in the FY 2027 General Appropriations Act.

Remove One-Time Site Condition Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,998,400) from the General Fund in FY 2027 for one-time funding related to the following projects approved by SFD:

Pima Unified 9-12 (FY 2023 School)

Queen Creek 9-12 (FY 2025 School)

\$(1,955,000)

\$(43,400)

New School Facilities (FY 2027 Authorization)

The Baseline includes \$38,809,400 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for one New School Facilities project which will be funded in FY 2027. Adjustments are as follows:

Agua Fria Construction Adjustment

The Baseline includes an increase of \$36,977,200 from the General Fund in FY 2027 to resolve OAH claims made by Agua Fria Union High School District regarding SFD's decision to "hold for consideration" the district's request for additional funding of a new high school above what SFD had previously awarded the district for FY 2024.

The \$36,977,200 is based on requested additional capacity of 783 students and the cost-per-square-foot rate that would have been applicable in FY 2024. While the Legislature typically appropriates only 50% of construction costs for New School Facilities projects in the first year, due to the terms of the settlement the Baseline includes the full \$36,977,200 amount to be funded in FY 2027.

A footnote in the FY 2026 General Appropriations Act states that it is the Legislature's intent that FY 2027 New School Facilities funding may include up to \$10,000,000 for end of useful life projects that receive final approval from SFD on or before December 15, 2025. The Baseline continues this footnote in FY 2027, which would apply to FY 2028 New School Facilities funding.

One-Time Site Condition Funding

The Baseline includes an increase of \$1,832,200 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for one-time funding related to the Agua Fria High School project that was funded in FY 2024.

Chino Valley Unified School District

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for construction in Chino Valley Unified School District. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Background – On August 7, 2024, SFD approved the retirement of 10,485 square feet from the Chino Valley High School building system. On December 13, 2024, SFD approved the construction of 9,200 square feet of new classroom space for Chino Valley High School at a cost of \$4,038,300. Pursuant to an FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote, SFD may use the unencumbered balance of \$18,117,400 in the New School Facilities Fund for this project, which resulted in the project receiving no direct General Fund appropriation in FY 2026.

Holbrook Unified School District

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for construction in Holbrook Unified School District. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Background – On August 7, 2024, SFD approved the retirement of 30,828 square feet from the Hulet Elementary School building system. The school district transferred 1st through 5th grade students from Hulet Elementary to Park Elementary. On December 13, 2024, SFD approved the construction of 5,100 square feet of new physical education space for Park Elementary School at a cost of \$2,281,500. Pursuant to an FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote, SFD may use the unencumbered balance of \$18,117,400 in the New School Facilities Fund for this project, which resulted in the project receiving no direct General Fund appropriation in FY 2026.

St. David Unified School District

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for construction in St. David Unified School District. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Background – On August 7, 2024, SFD approved the retirement of 5,214 square feet from the St. David High School building system. On December 13, 2024, SFD approved the construction of 4,300 square feet of new workshop space for St. David High School at a cost of \$1,797,600. Pursuant to an FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote, SFD may use the unencumbered balance of \$18,117,400 in the New School Facilities Fund for this project, which resulted in the project receiving no direct General Fund appropriation in FY 2026.

New School Facilities Debt Service

The Baseline includes \$9,938,100 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for New School Facilities Debt Service. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

SFD's only current debt service is for an FY 2010 leasepurchase agreement used to finance the costs of new school construction. That agreement requires the \$9,938,100 annual debt service payment through FY 2027 and a final lower debt service amount in FY 2028.

The FY 2027 Baseline includes \$9,938,100 for the debt service requirement for the 2010 Qualified School Construction Bonds (QSCB) issuance. The lease-purchase agreement associated with the QSCBs requires the state to appropriate the entire debt service amount for the payment, as opposed to deducting the expected federal subsidy from the payment. The state is expected to receive a federal subsidy of \$3,729,900 in FY 2027 related to the lease-purchase payment.

Pursuant to A.R.S. § 35-142.01, the subsidy funds will be deposited as revenue into the state General Fund, thereby leaving a net debt service obligation of \$6,208,200.

Building Renewal Grants Deposit

The Baseline includes \$16,667,900 from the General Fund in FY 2027 for Building Renewal Grants. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(183,300,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for building renewal grants.

Since FY 2014, the state has funded an ongoing "base" amount of Building Renewal Grant funding of \$16,667,900. (See Table 2.)

Background – SFD distributes monies to school districts to fund “primary” building renewal projects. SFD prioritizes projects with emphasis given to school districts that have provided routine preventative maintenance. “Primary” building renewal projects are those required to meet the minimum adequacy guidelines. Statute also requires SFD to prioritize funding to critical projects.

Pursuant to A.R.S. § 41-5721, SFD is required to transfer excess funds in the New School Facilities (NSF) Fund to the Emergency Deficiencies Correction (EDC) Fund to the extent that the transfer does not affect or disrupt any approved new construction projects.

If there are insufficient monies in the EDC Fund for district requests, A.R.S. § 15-907 allows a district to levy an additional primary property tax to fund the repairs, with the approval of the respective County Board of Supervisors.

Building Renewal Grants Administration

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Building Renewal Grants Administration. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(750,000) and (5) FTE Positions from the General Fund to remove one-time funding for operating costs associated with the administration of the Building Renewal Grant program. The FY 2026 General Appropriations Act made these monies non-lapsing.

Long-Term Budget Impacts

As part of the Baseline's 3-year spending plan, SFD’s General Fund costs are projected to increase by \$995,300 in FY 2028 above FY 2027 and increase by \$21,669,600 in FY 2029 above FY 2028. These estimates are based on:

New School Construction

The long-term estimates assume 2 types of new school construction funding: 1) Providing the remaining funding in FY 2028 for the schools which were authorized to begin construction in FY 2027; and 2) Conceptual approvals made by SFD as part of the agency's long-term planning process.

In FY 2028, new school construction spending is projected to increase by \$3,449,900. FY 2028 projects are as follows:

Buckeye Elementary (K-8) – for a new elementary school.

Buckeye Union (9-12) – for a new high school, including land.

Marana (9-12) – for a new high school.

• Maricopa (9-12) – for a high school addition.

• Nadaburg (9-12) – for a high school addition.

In addition, FY 2029 new school construction spending is projected to increase by \$29,153,100. Projects are as follows:

Queen Creek (9-12) – for a high school addition.

Saddle Mountain (9-12) – for a high school addition.

Somerton (K-6) – for a new elementary school, including a land donation credit.

New construction projects assumed to start in FY 2028 and FY 2029 reflect SFD conceptual approvals as of December 2025.

New School Facilities Debt Service

SFD new school facilities debt service funding would decrease by \$(2,454,600) in FY 2028 below FY 2027. This decrease represents the lower amount in the final year of SFD's debt service schedule for an FY 2010 lease-purchase agreement used to finance the costs of new school construction.

This debt service funding would further decrease by \$(7,483,500) in FY 2029 below FY 2028 to reflect the conclusion of payments for this long-term debt.

Lease to Own Debt Service Fund (SFA2373/A.R.S. § 41-5704) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Appropriated monies and interest earnings from the investment of lease-to-own Certificates of Participation proceeds.

New School Facilities Debt Service

Purpose of Fund: To pay the debt service on any lease-to-own agreements entered into by the school facilities oversight board to finance the costs of new school construction. General Fund appropriation expenditures are not displayed to avoid double counting of appropriations.

New School Facilities Fund (SFA2460/A.R.S. § 41-5731) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Appropriated monies, monies received by the State Land Department from the lease of state public school land, and proceeds from lease-to-own agreements. General Fund appropriation expenditures are not displayed to avoid double counting of appropriations.

Purpose of Fund: To provide school districts with monies for constructing new school facilities, and to pay for the following: construction project management services, school building structural assessments, and land acquisition.

School Improvement Revenue Bond Debt Service Fund (SFA5020/A.R.S. § 41-5084) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Revenues from a 0.6% increase in the state Transaction Privilege Tax (as approved under Proposition 301 in the 2000 General Election) and monies credited to the fund from the Permanent State School Fund.
